issues.body: The new text says account issue titles are static configuration edited by a maintainer and that a raw handle appears on “no generated surface at all,” including no generated log line, issue body, or alert. At the current PR head, `.github/workflows/set-up-account.yml` computes `HANDLE=[redacted-account]`, creates the account issue with `gh issue create --title "$HANDLE"`, emits multiple `echo`/error lines containing `$HANDLE`, creates policy PR text containing the handle, and posts request/account comments containing `$HANDLE`. Those are machine-generated public surfaces, not hand-edited static configuration. The narrower fingerprint guarantees in model-health, dashboard-gen, and lease parsing do not establish the universal invariant asserted here.
issues.fix_hint: Describe the actual scoped invariant precisely: identify which generated identity-bearing ledger/health/dashboard/diagnostic surfaces require fingerprints, while explicitly retaining the enrollment/account-catalog surfaces that intentionally expose handles. Alternatively, implementing a repo-wide no-generated-handle invariant would require code changes across set-up-account and its consumers, with non-vacuous seam tests; prose alone cannot establish it.
issues.title: Universal no-generated-handle claim contradicts the enrollment workflow

verdict.summary: The documentation change overstates the implemented privacy boundary. The repository does enforce salted fingerprints on several named ledger/dashboard paths, but it does not enforce the new universal claim that raw handles occur only in hand-edited static configuration and on no generated surface. A current enrollment workflow generates public issues, comments, PR text, and Actions log lines containing the raw handle. Because this paragraph declares the code-backed security contract and says widening it requires a locked decision, documenting a materially stronger invariant than the code provides is not sound.
